pure-announcement.rationale: It is release coverage, but it carries ideas that transfer beyond Bumblebee: the SBOM/EDR blind spot for on-disk developer state, and the principle that a supply-chain scanner must never invoke package managers because postinstall scripts would trigger the very attack it checks for.

duplicate.rationale: Shadow-mcp-detection and siem-agentic-visibility-gap concern unsanctioned MCP servers and telemetry gaps, not read-only inventory of package, extension, and MCP-config state on developer endpoints.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The tool is public on GitHub under Apache 2.0, so every mechanism claim in the note is directly checkable.

durability.rationale: Much of the note is v0.1-bound specifics — unsupported bun.lockb, exact config filename lists, Go 1.25 requirement, current ecosystem matrix — that will churn, even though the dev-endpoint blind-spot framing is durable.

actionability.rationale: The concrete steps are product-specific (install command, scan profiles, catalog format); the transferable never-execute-installers principle is real but stated in passing rather than developed into guidance.

atomicity.rationale: The note states one idea cleanly: answer 'which developer machines are exposed right now' by read-only scanning of on-disk package, extension, and AI-tool-config metadata.
